description:
# Dynmap for PowerNukkitX **A live, Google Maps style web map of your Bedrock server, powered by [Dynmap](https://github.com/webbukkit/dynmap) and running natively on [PowerNukkitX](https://github.com/PowerNukkitX/PowerNukkitX).** [![Build](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/actions/workflows/build.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/actions/workflows/build.yml) [![Docker](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/actions/workflows/docker.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/actions/workflows/docker.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx?include_prereleases&sort=semver)](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/releases) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx)](LICENSE) ![Java 21](https://img.shields.io/badge/java-21-orange) ![PowerNukkitX 3.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/PowerNukkitX-3.0-blue)
--- ## Contents * [Why](#why) * [Features](#features) * [Compatibility](#compatibility) * [Installation](#installation) * [Running with Docker](#running-with-docker) * [Usage](#usage) * [Configuration](#configuration) * [How it works](#how-it-works) * [Known limitations](#known-limitations) * [Building from source](#building-from-source) * [Contributing](#contributing) * [Credits and license](#credits-and-license) ## Why Dynmap is the classic web map for Java Edition servers, but it never had a Bedrock server port. PowerNukkitX is a full featured Bedrock server written in Java, so DynmapCore can run inside it with a thin bridge. This project is that bridge: it feeds PNX worlds, chunks, players and events into an unmodified DynmapCore, so you get the same web map, renderers and marker API you know from Bukkit. ## Features * 🗺️ **Full Dynmap web UI** on port `8123`: flat, surface and cave maps, zoom, day/night lighting. * 🧱 **Native block mapping**: every PowerNukkitX block state is registered with Dynmap at startup. Bedrock block ids line up with the Java names Dynmap's colour schemes use, so vanilla blocks get proper colours out of the box. * 🌍 **Multi world**: overworld, nether and the end are detected from the level dimension, including worlds loaded or unloaded at runtime. * ⚡ **Live updates**: placing and breaking blocks invalidates the affected tiles immediately. * 👥 **Player tracking**: players, health and armor show up on the map in real time. * 💬 **Chat bridge**: in game chat appears on the web map and web chat is broadcast to the server. * 📍 **Markers and commands**: `/dynmap`, `/dmap`, `/dmarker` and `/dynmapexp` work as they do on other platforms. * 🐳 **Docker image** with PowerNukkitX and the plugin preinstalled. ## Compatibility | Component | Version | |---|---| | PowerNukkitX | 3.0.x (built against `3.0.0-SNAPSHOT`) | | Plugin API (`api` in plugin.yml) | 1.0.0 | | Dynmap core | 3.9-SNAPSHOT, pinned commit in [`gradle.properties`](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/blob/main/gradle.properties) | | Java | 21 | ## Installation 1. Download `Dynmap--pnx.jar` from the [latest release](https://github.com/xRookieFight/dynmap-pnx/releases). 2. Put it into the `plugins/` folder of your PowerNukkitX server. 3. Start the server once. Dynmap creates `plugins/dynmap/` with its configuration and web files. 4. Open `http://:8123` in a browser. 5. Run `/dynmap fullrender ` from the console to render existing terrain. New chunks render on their own as players explore. > [!TIP] > If you are behind a firewall or a hosting panel, open TCP port `8123` in addition to the usual UDP `19132`. ## Running with Docker The image bundles a PowerNukkitX server with the plugin already in place. The plugin jar is copied into `/data/plugins` on every start, so updating the image updates the plugin. ```bash docker run -d --name pnx-dynmap \ -p 19132:19132/udp \ -p 8123:8123 \ -v pnx-data:/data \ -it ghcr.io/xrookiefight/dynmap-pnx:latest ``` With Docker Compose: ```yaml services: pnx: image: ghcr.io/xrookiefight/dynmap-pnx:latest container_name: pnx-dynmap stdin_open: true tty: true ports: - "19132:19132/udp" - "8123:8123" volumes: - ./data:/data environment: JAVA_OPTS: "-Xms2G -Xmx4G -XX:+UseZGC -XX:+ZGenerational" restart: unless-stopped ``` Attach to the console with `docker attach pnx-dynmap` (detach with `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+Q`). To build the image yourself: ```bash docker build -t dynmap-pnx . docker build --build-arg PNX_VERSION=3.0.1-SNAPSHOT -t dynmap-pnx . ``` | Build argument | Default | Purpose | |---|---|---| | `JAVA_VERSION` | `21` | Temurin base image version | | `PNX_VERSION` | `3.0.0-SNAPSHOT` | PowerNukkitX server build to bundle | | `PNX_REPOSITORY` | `https://repo.powernukkitx.org/releases` | Maven repository to fetch PNX from | The Dockerfile clones Dynmap at the commit pinned in `gradle.properties`, so the build is reproducible and needs nothing but Docker. ## Usage | Command | What it does | |---|---| | `/dynmap render` | Render the area around you | | `/dynmap fullrender ` | Render a whole world | | `/dynmap radiusrender ` | Render a radius around you | | `/dynmap cancelrender ` | Stop a running render | | `/dynmap pause all` | Pause all rendering | | `/dynmap stats` | Render statistics | | `/dynmap hide` / `show` | Hide or show yourself on the map | | `/dmap worldlist` | List worlds and their maps | | `/dmarker add
